title: Place a core row past the agreement radius p^26 (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4490 uses `||B - P|| < p^6 exp(-p^2)` on one core axis. Does a core row kept at distance `A = ceil(p^{48})` from every face lie past the within-cell agreement radius of #4452?

## Result

Let `p ≥ 2` and `0 ≤ W ≤ p - 1`. The bandwidth `R = (2 p^{24} - 1) W` satisfies `R < p^{26}`, because

```text
p^{26} - (2 p^{24} - 1)(p - 1) = p^{24} ((p - 1)^2 + 1) + p - 1 > 0.
```

For an integer `p`, `A = p^{48}`, and `p^{48} = p^{26} p^{22}` with `p^{22} ≥ 2^{22} > 1`. Thus `R < p^{26} < A`. The core row is strictly outside that bandwidth, so its section-polynomial row is the global polynomial row. Under the #4452 gauge, `||P - H_sec^{-1}||_2 < p^6 exp(-p^2)`.

Distance `p^{25}` fails: at `p = 2` the loose radius is `2^{25} + 1`.

**Claim type:** one distance comparison. **No new κ.** The ideal gaps stay hypotheses, and the operator bound is not re-proved. The #4100 notes still use `p^{10} exp(-p^2)`.

The locality audit already says `A` clears the written radius for `J = ceil(p^{42})`. This comparison is against the lowered radius `p^{26}`.

This branch starts from canonical main. It does not replay #4452.
